Iraq alone, in the Kingdom's line: 434,052 km2 against the infobox's 438,317 km2 (ratio 0.99). When the Arab Federation ended is for the arab-federation dossier; the Iraq page does not mention it.

correction.text: unchanged: Iraq without the neutral zone; holds 1960 to 1981

keyframe_review.note: 1960-1982, 434,052 km2 (ratio 0.99 to the infobox's 438,317 km2): Iraq without its share of the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone, a 'kite-shaped region of 7,044 km2' created by the Protocol of Uqair (2 December 1922). The shape is right to 1981; the zone was divided in 1982 (see the 1982 keyframe), and the cells Cliopatria adds in 1991 (22 cells at about 29.1-29.5 N, 44.2-46.4 E) are Iraq's share.

correction.text: Iraq with its share of the former neutral zone

Iraq with its share, which is the 1991 shape (the 1991 shape differs from the 1960 shape by these 22 cells and one more). The page also says 'Administrative division of the zone was achieved in 1975', which moves no cell here.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1983 shape plus Iraq's share of the former neutral zone; the four cells east of Basra stay out, unverified

keyframe_review.note: 1983-1986, 433,250 km2: the 1960 shape less four cells (about 1,000 km2) at 47.8-48.1 E, 30.6-31.0 N east of Basra, which no page opened names. The Iran-Iraq War page dates Iranian gains only to Haj Omran (23 July 1983), Dawn 4 (September 1983, 'about 15 km' into Iraq) and Majnoon Island (February 1984), so the cut is unverified. The neutral-zone share is added (see 1982). Holds 1983-1986 as Cliopatria has it.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1987 shape plus Iraq's share of the former neutral zone; holds 1987 to August 1988, not 1989

keyframe_review.note: 1987-1989, 431,905 km2: the 1983 shape less five more cells, three on the Iranian border in Kurdistan (about 36.0-36.2 N, 45.1-45.4 E) and two in the marshes east of al-Qurnah (about 47.7 E, 30.7-30.9 N). The page puts Iranian ground in Iraq at Haj Omran (23 July 1983), Dawn 4 (September 1983) and Majnoon Island with 'the marshes' (captured 'By 27 February' 1984); it dates the end to the cease-fire of August 1988 and says 'The war did not create any permanent border changes', so the shape is right for 1987-1988 only. The neutral-zone share is added.

correction.text: Iraq in its pre-war line with the neutral-zone share, after the cease-fire of 20 August 1988

correction.text: Iraq without Kuwait, the 19th governorate of Iraqi claim, held as occupied land

keyframe_review.note: 1990, 456,521 km2: the 1991 shape plus exactly the 62 cells of Kuwait. The Iraq page says 'On 2 August 1990, the Iraqi forces invaded and annexed Kuwait as its 19th governorate'; the annexation was not recognised, so Kuwait is drawn as occupied land (hatched, from the Kuwaiti dossier's keyframe and the occupation events) and cut from the Iraqi shape.

correction.text: unchanged: Iraq within its present line; holds 1991 only

keyframe_review.note: 1991-1999, 439,074 km2 against the infobox's 438,317 km2 (ratio 1.00). Holds for 1991 only; from 1992 the three Kurdish governorates are out of Baghdad's hands (see the 1992 keyframe). The Iraq-Kuwait border page says the UN demarcation, referred to the United Nations in July 1992 and accepted by Iraq in November 1994, 'followed the 1932 line with some minor adjustments' and names no land, so no cell is moved for it.

correction.text: Iraq without the three governorates of the de facto Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1992-1999: 'the autonomous region was de facto established in 1992' (infobox 'Autonomy founded: 19 May 1992'), with the no-fly zones of March 1991. The page lists Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok among the region's governorates (and a fourth, Halabja, not entered separately); Kirkuk is not among them and the page calls it disputed, with Peshmerga taking it only after Iraqi forces withdrew in the 2014 period. The region is drawn as the three governorates; the page's infobox gives 46,862 km2 for the whole region.

correction.text: Iraq without the three Kurdish governorates, 2000 to 15 October 2005

keyframe_review.note: 2000-2005, the same 439,074 km2 shape as 1991-1999, but the Kurdistan Region stayed outside Baghdad's control until the constitution of 15 October 2005 ('Federal region established: 15 October 2005'; 'The Iraqi government only recognized the Kurdistan Region as a federal region in 2005'). The shape holds 2000 to September 2005; the October 2005 gain returns the region. The page gives no date for the 2003 occupation, so no hatch is drawn for 2003-2004 (page budget).

ledger.note: 14 July 1958: a coup led by Abdul Karim Qasim overthrows the monarchy and Iraq becomes a republic. Infobox 'Republic declared: 14 July 1958'; 'in 1958 a military coup led by Abdul Karim Qasim overthrew the monarchy and established a republic'.
February 1963: the Ba'ath party takes power in a coup. The page dates the Ba'ath takeover to a 'February 1963 coup' (the day is not on the page). Same state, same land, new regime.
17 July 1968: the Ba'ath returns to power. 'The 17 July Revolution overthrew Arif and brought the Iraqi Ba'ath Party to power in 1968.' Same state, same land, new regime.

region.text: the Shatt al-Arab and its eastern bank, where the frontier moved to the river's thalweg

ledger.note: 1975: Iraq cedes the eastern bank of the Shatt al-Arab to Iran under the Algiers Agreement. Saddam's invasion of 1980 aimed in part 'to retake the eastern bank of the Shatt al-Arab, which it had ceded in the 1975 Algiers Agreement'; the Iraq page adds that it was 'signed in 1975 by Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Saddam' and that Iran withdrew its support for the Kurds. The ceded strip is narrow, a few cells at the grid's resolution.

region.text: Khuzestan, Mehran and the ground forward of Qasr-e Shirin, where Iraq held Iranian land from 1980

ledger.note: 22 September 1980: Iraq invades Iran along 'a 644 km front'. Iraq sent four divisions into Khuzestan 'to cut off the Shatt al-Arab from the rest of Iran', occupied Mehran, took most of Khorramshahr by 24 October and secured ground 'forward of Qasr-e Shirin'; on 10 September Iraq had already 'forcibly reclaimed territories in Zain al-Qaws and Saif Saad', the page does not say where. The zone is the border land in Iran that Iraq held or fought for until June 1982.

region.text: Iraq's share of the former neutral zone, as the 22 cells Cliopatria adds in 1991; the page does not say how the zone was divided

ledger.note: 1982: Iraq takes its share of the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone. 'An agreement to partition the neutral zone was reached by Iraqi and Saudi representatives on 26 December 1981', 'approved by the Iraqi National Assembly on 28 January 1982', and 'the territory was divided on an unknown date between 28 January and 30 July 1982'. The zone (7,044 km2, from the Protocol of Uqair of 2 December 1922) was neutral, held by neither side, so the counterpart is nobody. The page does not say how it was split, so the region is the cells Cliopatria adds between its 1960 and 1991 shapes.

region.text: the Iranian land Iraq held from 1980, retaken by June 1982

ledger.note: June 1982: Iran retakes its land. The Khorramshahr offensive began on 23 May 1982 and the city fell in under 48 hours; Iran 'recaptured all their territory by June 1982'. On 20 June Saddam offered a cease-fire and withdrawal 'within two weeks' and Khomeini rejected it; Iraq kept 'some border areas, notably the Shatt al-Arab'.

region.text: the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and the border ground round it, held by Iran

ledger.note: 23 July 1983: Iran takes the Iraqi town of Haj Omran. 'With Kurdish support, Iran captured the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and held it'; in September 1983 Operation Dawn 4 gained 'some Iraqi land' before Iraq stopped it 'about 15 km' in. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): type changed from contest_start to occupation_start: the Iran-Iraq War page has Iran capture the place and hold it ('captured the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and held it'; Majnoon 'By 27 February' 1984, then kept), which is an occupation of Iraqi land; islamic-republic-of-iran records Majnoon as occupation_start (1984-2) and occupation_end (1988-8).

region.text: Majnoon Island and the marshes along it, held by Iran

ledger.note: February 1984: Iran takes Majnoon Island. Operation Kheibar (24 February to 19 March 1984): Iran captured Majnoon Island 'By 27 February' and after retreating from Qurna 'still held onto' the marshes 'along with Majnoon Island'. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): type changed from contest_start to occupation_start: the Iran-Iraq War page has Iran capture the place and hold it ('captured the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and held it'; Majnoon 'By 27 February' 1984, then kept), which is an occupation of Iraqi land; islamic-republic-of-iran records Majnoon as occupation_start (1984-2) and occupation_end (1988-8).

region.text: the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and the border ground round it, held by Iran from 1983

ledger.note: 20 August 1988: the cease-fire ends the Iran-Iraq War and Haj Omran returns to the pre-war line. The infobox gives '22 September 1980 - 20 August 1988', result 'Inconclusive', territorial changes 'Status quo ante bellum'; the text says the cease-fire 'became effective in August 1988' after Security Council Resolution 598 and that 'The war did not create any permanent border changes'. Which ground each side held at the cease-fire is not on the page. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): type changed from contest_end to occupation_end: the Iran-Iraq War page has Iran capture the place and hold it ('captured the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and held it'; Majnoon 'By 27 February' 1984, then kept), which is an occupation of Iraqi land; islamic-republic-of-iran records Majnoon as occupation_start (1984-2) and occupation_end (1988-8). Confidence lowered to 2: the page dates the cease-fire (20 August 1988) and says the war made no permanent border changes, but does not say when this ground went back to Iraq.

region.text: Majnoon Island and the marshes along it, held by Iran from 1984

ledger.note: 20 August 1988: the cease-fire ends the Iran-Iraq War and Majnoon Island returns to the pre-war line ('Status quo ante bellum'; 'The war did not create any permanent border changes'). The pages opened do not say when Iraq retook the island, only that no border changed. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): type changed from contest_end to occupation_end: the Iran-Iraq War page has Iran capture the place and hold it ('captured the Iraqi town of Haj Omran and held it'; Majnoon 'By 27 February' 1984, then kept), which is an occupation of Iraqi land; islamic-republic-of-iran records Majnoon as occupation_start (1984-2) and occupation_end (1988-8). Confidence lowered to 2: the page dates the cease-fire (20 August 1988) and says the war made no permanent border changes, but does not say when this ground went back to Iraq.

2 August 1990: Iraq invades and annexes Kuwait. 'On 2 August 1990, the Iraqi forces invaded and annexed Kuwait as its 19th governorate.' The annexation was not recognised, so Kuwait is drawn as occupied land, not as Iraqi.

26 February 1991: the Iraqi occupation of Kuwait ends. 'The Iraqi occupation of Kuwait ended on 26 February 1991' (the infobox gives 28 February); the Iraq page describes a coalition ground assault that 'lasted 100 hours'. Kuwait is restored (the 'kuwait' row).

region.text: the Kurdistan Region of 1992: the governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok

ledger.note: 1992: Baghdad loses control of Iraqi Kurdistan. 'the autonomous region was de facto established in 1992' (infobox 'Autonomy founded: 19 May 1992'), after the no-fly zones of March 1991 and Election Act No. 1 of 8 April 1992; the first elections were on 19 May 1992. The Iraq page says 'autonomy was given to Kurds' after the 1991 uprisings, which 'were repressed'. Kirkuk is not among the region's governorates and the Kurdistan page calls it disputed. The month is that of the elections.

region.text: Iraq without the Kurdistan Region, which keeps its own land

ledger.note: 2005: Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic row ends and its 'Republic of Iraq' row resumes only in 2014. Not the end of a state: the state continues under the constitution of 15 October 2005, which the page gives as the current one; the end date is a row boundary bridged by the researcher. [fx-43 R149] The region excludes the three governorates of the Kurdistan Region: the former ledger/14 (2005-10 gain of the Region from kurdistan-region) is dropped, because no land changes hands. Kurdistan Region page: the constitution of 15 October 2005 'recognizes the Kurdistan Region as a federal region while preserving its existing authorities established in 1992' ('the autonomous region was de facto established in 1992'); the Region stays in the kurdistan-region dossier, and data/hierarchy.csv draws it as a constituent of republic-of-iraq from 2005. Dropped note: 15 October 2005: the Kurdistan Region becomes a federal region of Iraq. wars.name: Kuwait crisis of 1961 (Operation Vantage)
wars.outcome: Iraq threatened to invade Kuwait in July 1961; the invasion 'was finally averted following plans by the Arab League to form an international Arab force' and British forces had withdrawn by 19 October.
wars.note: A threat, not a campaign; no ground was taken.

Haj Omran and Majnoon Island with the marshes, held by Iran from 1983 and 1984

wars.outcome: Inconclusive: 22 September 1980 to 20 August 1988, 'Status quo ante bellum'; 'The war did not create any permanent border changes'.
wars.note: The pages opened do not cover al-Faw (1986), Halabja (1988) or the Basra front, so Iranian gains there are not entered.

wars.name: Invasion of Kuwait and Gulf War

zones.text: the whole of Kuwait, 2 August 1990 to 26 February 1991

wars.outcome: Iraq annexed Kuwait on 2 August 1990 as its 19th governorate; a US-led coalition ground assault of 100 hours ended the occupation on 26 February 1991.

wars.name: 1991 Iraqi uprisings and the no-fly zones

zones.text: the Kurdish governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok

wars.outcome: The uprisings 'were repressed', but the US, UK, Turkey and France set up the Iraqi no-fly zones under Security Council Resolution 688 and 'autonomy was given to Kurds': the Kurdistan Region was de facto established in 1992.
wars.note: The Kurdistan page dates the no-fly zones to March 1991 and the autonomy to 19 May 1992.

wars.name: 2003 invasion of Iraq
wars.outcome: 'On 20 March 2003, the US-led coalition invaded Iraq'; the Kurdistan page says it 'overthrew Saddam Hussein'. The occupation and the Coalition Provisional Authority are not dated on the pages opened, so no occupation is entered.
wars.note: Gap: the occupation of 2003-2004 would be hatched under rule 4; a page for the Coalition Provisional Authority is needed.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow treaty and survey lines (the 1932 Kuwait line, the Algiers Agreement line of 1975 on the Shatt al-Arab). Exceptions: the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone, shared and undefined until 1982 (soft), and the front lines of 1980-1988.

National frontiers as before, after the UN demarcation of the Kuwait border (accepted November 1994); the line of the de facto Kurdistan Region, held from 1992, is a front, not a survey: soft, and Kirkuk stayed disputed.

notes: Written by me-10-k on 2026-10-25 from six pages (a seventh, the Iraq-Saudi Arabia border page, was opened first and replaced by the neutral-zone page, which dates the division). SAME STATE AS 'republic-of-iraq' (Wikidata Q796): Iraq from 1958 to today is one state; Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic (1960-2005) and Republic of Iraq (2014-2024) rows leave 2006-2013 empty. The brief would have the earlier slug carry both Names, but the later row belongs to another part (me-10-m), so this dossier stops at the row boundary; its end is a confidence-1 dissolve and republic-of-iraq must start in 2005/2006 or the gap-filler must join them (the Iraq row for 2006-2013 is the one thing missing from the map). Cliopatria's 1958-1959 years are covered by its Arab Federation row (Iraq and Jordan), which is wrong for Iraq after 14 July 1958: new keyframe 1958-1959. Neutral zone: the pages give 1975 as an 'administrative division' and 1982 as the territorial partition; the Saudi dossier (another group) also uses 1982 with counterpart nobody. Gazetteer names needed: Haj Omran, Mehran, Majnoon Island (places), none of which the gazetteer has; Khuzestan, the Shatt al-Arab and the Arbil/As-Sulaymaniyah/Dihok governorates resolve. GAPS (page budget): the 2003-2004 occupation under the Coalition Provisional Authority (rule 4 hatch); al-Faw (1986-1988), Halabja and the Basra front; the 1993 UN demarcation (land not named); the 1991 uprising in the south. The 1983 and 1987 Cliopatria cuts (four cells east of Basra; three Kurdish-border and two marsh cells) are only partly explained by the pages. KURDISTAN: the counterpart 'kurdistan-region' needs a dossier (Kurdistan Regional Government, de facto state 1992-2005, federal region after); I made it a loss in 1992 and a gain in October 2005 because Baghdad had no control in between; if the project prefers to keep Iraq's shape solid with a vassal tint, change those two events. Rulers not entered: no page opened gives the list.
